text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Economic Development Board has pledged to get tough with scholars who break their bonds, even as it launched its first batch of Singapore Inc scholarships yesterday.
- A company listed on the Stock Exchange of Singapore was raided by the police and representatives of the software industry's watchdog, on suspicion of software piracy.
- King Norodom Sihanouk said Cambodian strongman Hun Sen had rejected his offer to abdicate and that no friction was encountered during the audience he granted to the Second Prime Minister.
- Former television actor Tay Chin Seng, accused of molesting his maid, failed to appear for a court hearing.
- Singapore Airlines said it had no immediate plans to merge its local and foreign shares, a development which ought to cheer up holders of its foreign tranche shares.

- Home loans growth in the second quarter shrank to a single-digit figure for the first time since 1980 -- a far cry from the heady growth rates exceeding 20 percent before the property speculation curbs in May last year.
- The Singapore Technologies group has merged the dual listings of four companies with "local" and "foreign" tranches, capping a topsy-turvy week for shareholders.
- Hedge funds controlled by George Soros and other big players could have made US$1 billion each speculating on the Thai baht and other struggling Asian currencies, traders estimated.
- Advanced Systems Automation, which last posted a turnover of S$88 million, is aiming high -- S$500 million sales in three years to be specific.
- United Overseas Land and its partners, United Overseas Bank and Singapore Land, will spend S$780 million to develop its flagship property, Novena Square.

- Singapore Telecom shares lost ground in relatively heavy trading and closed at the week's low of S$2.48, two cents below the price at which CPF members were offered SingTel shares under last year's ST2 share offer.
- Listed ABR Holdings has postponed its plan to buy a stake in PT Aneka Food Tatarasa Industri as the Indonesian firm's performance has not met expectations.
- Listed Superior Metal Printing yesterday posted a 25.5 percent rise in interim net profit of S$767,000.
